epa_lmop.terms_note: EPA's data catalog lists 'All Landfills in LMOP Database with Coordinates' under the EPA Standard Open Data License. LMOP lists municipal solid waste landfills only: no open dumps, transfer stations, recycling centres, industrial or hazardous waste landfills. No source of open dumps or other solid waste facilities in Puerto Rico states terms (wanted.json: open-dumps).

hud_chas.name: HUD — Comprehensive Housing Affordability Strategy (CHAS) data by census tract
hud_chas.publisher: US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Office of Policy Development and Research (eGIS); tabulated by the US Census Bureau

more_links.label: CHAS by tract feature service (the build reads layer 1)
HUD open data catalog (DCAT, states the licence)
CHAS on HUD User (newer releases; refuses scripted downloads)

hud_chas.licence: U.S. Public Domain (the licence HUD's open data catalog gives this dataset: the usa.gov public domain label); HUD adds a disclaimer of warranty and liability
hud_chas.credit: Source: US Department of Housing and Urban Development, Comprehensive Housing Affordability Strategy (CHAS) data, 2016-2020 ACS 5-year, census tracts (HUD eGIS), downloaded October 2026
hud_chas.access: ArcGIS REST query of HUD's eGIS layer (no key), STATE = '72': the tract id and three counts of Table 2 (all households; owners and renters with one or more of the four severe housing problems). The release (Date of Coverage) is read from the item's description.
hud_chas.cadence: HUD releases a new CHAS window about once a year on HUD User; the eGIS layer lags (2016-2020 on 2026-10-17, while HUD User has 2018-2022). The observatory re-reads the layer when the conditions unit is rebuilt (python conditions.py --refresh chas), and the freshness check watches the layer for a new release.
hud_chas.used_for: Households with one or more severe housing problems and their share, by municipio (exact) and by barrio (an estimate spread from tracts by 2020 housing units) (conditions_series.json and conditions_barrio.json: chas_severe_hh, chas_severe_pct).
hud_chas.terms_note: HUD User's CHAS downloads (2018-2022, published December 2025) sit behind a bot check that refuses scripts, as its LIHTC, Fair Market Rent and Income Limits files do; the observatory does not get around it. The eGIS layer is the newest release a script may read. Counts in CHAS are rounded by the Census Bureau, and the layer publishes no margins of error.

census_tiger_lines.name: US Census Bureau — TIGER/Line Shapefiles, all lines (EDGES)

more_links.label: TIGER/Line 2026 EDGES files (the build reads the 78 Puerto Rico files)

census_tiger_lines.credit: Source: US Census Bureau, 2026 TIGER/Line Shapefiles, all lines (EDGES), Puerto Rico
census_tiger_lines.access: The 78 county files of the newest TIGER/Line year (no key; about 55 MB zipped), read with pyshp. The build keeps, for each road edge (ROADFLG = 'Y'), its id, feature class (MTFCC), its two topological nodes and their points.
census_tiger_lines.cadence: The Census Bureau publishes a TIGER/Line year each autumn. The observatory finds the newest year itself when the conditions unit is rebuilt (python conditions.py --refresh tiger).
census_tiger_lines.used_for: Street intersections and their density per square mile, by barrio and municipio (conditions_series.json and conditions_barrio.json: street_intersections, street_intersection_density).

hhs_hospital_capacity.name: HHS — COVID-19 Reported Patient Impact and Hospital Capacity by Facility (geocoded hospital addresses)
hhs_hospital_capacity.publisher: US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), healthdata.gov

more_links.label: Socrata API of the dataset (the build reads ccn and geocoded_hospital_address)

hhs_hospital_capacity.licence: Public Domain U.S. Government (as healthdata.gov states for the dataset)
hhs_hospital_capacity.credit: Source: US Department of Health and Human Services, COVID-19 Reported Patient Impact and Hospital Capacity by Facility (geocoded hospital addresses, last reported April 2024)
hhs_hospital_capacity.access: The dataset's Socrata API (no key): for Puerto Rico, each hospital's certification number and HHS's geocoded point, the last week it reported. Only the point is kept, in the local cache: it places the hospitals OpenStreetMap does not, it is where the build looks for the OpenStreetMap building of a hospital whose name matches only in part, and for the hospitals OpenStreetMap places by name it shows how far HHS's point lies from the building. Nothing from HHS is published.
hhs_hospital_capacity.cadence: HHS stopped updating the dataset on 2024-05-03, so it is never re-checked. Hospitals rarely move; a new hospital it lacks is located by OpenStreetMap or by hand (conditions.HAND_POINTS).
hhs_hospital_capacity.used_for: The point of 15 of the 52 general hospitals the drive time is measured to, and the place where the build finds the OpenStreetMap building of 8 more (conditions_series.json and conditions_barrio.json: hosp_drive_min, hosp_road_km). The points are cached locally and never published.
hhs_hospital_capacity.terms_note: HHS geocoded street addresses; for the 27 hospitals OpenStreetMap places by name, HHS's point lies a median 0.7 km and up to 5.6 km from the building, and in another barrio for 13 of them. That is why OpenStreetMap is tried first, and why which barrios show 0 minutes is uncertain near the 15 hospitals placed at HHS's point.

nps_nrhp.name: National Park Service — National Register of Historic Places, public locations
nps_nrhp.publisher: National Park Service (NPS), Cultural Resources GIS, for the National Register of Historic Places

more_links.label: Map service (the build reads layers 0, points, and 1, polygons)

nps_nrhp.licence: Public domain: a US federal government work. NPS states no named licence; the map service's licence field says 'For general public distribution' and its metadata calls the public data general reference data. Treated as public domain, as other federal data are (decided by FPR on 2026-10-18)
nps_nrhp.credit: Source: National Park Service, National Register of Historic Places, public spatial data
nps_nrhp.access: ArcGIS REST queries (no key) of layer 0 (points) and layer 1 (polygons), State = 'PUERTO RICO'. The build keeps the reference number, name, resource type, city, listing date, status and one point (for a listing with only a polygon, a point inside it); the street address is never requested.
nps_nrhp.cadence: NPS edits the data as properties are listed (Data.gov: updated 2026-09-18; the newest Puerto Rico edit was 2026-08-07 and the newest listing 2026-01). The observatory re-reads it when the data are rebuilt (python community_assets.py --refresh nps).
nps_nrhp.used_for: Historic places on the 2D map (historic_places.geojson) and their count in each municipio (community_series.json: nrhp_places).
nps_nrhp.terms_note: Restricted and sensitive listings, such as archaeological sites, are not in the public data. NPS says the data are for general reference: using them does not satisfy consultation under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, and the points and outlines can be imprecise (most points come from the nomination's coordinates). NPS gives no warranty and asks users to get the data from its own servers. Private residences, and listings whose name holds a street address or house number, are counted in their municipio but not drawn, and their names are not published (decided by FPR on 2026-10-18; the reviewed list is nrhp_review.json in the repository). No address is published.

samhsa_nsumhss.name: SAMHSA — National Directories of substance use and mental health treatment facilities (N-SUMHSS)
samhsa_nsumhss.publisher: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), Center for Behavioral Health Statistics and Quality

more_links.label: 2025 National Directory of Drug and Alcohol Use Treatment Facilities (Excel and PDF)
2025 National Directory of Mental Health Treatment Facilities (Excel and PDF)
FindTreatment.gov (the live locator; not used, see the note)

samhsa_nsumhss.licence: Public domain: the directories carry SAMHSA's Public Domain Notice (they may be reproduced or copied without permission; citation is appreciated; they may not be reproduced or distributed for a fee without SAMHSA's written authorization)
samhsa_nsumhss.credit: Source: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration, 2025 National Directories of Drug and Alcohol Use and of Mental Health Treatment Facilities (2024 National Substance Use and Mental Health Services Survey)
samhsa_nsumhss.access: The Excel file of each directory, found on SAMHSA's National Directories page (no key), read in memory. For each Puerto Rico row the build keeps the city, the state, the type-of-care codes (substance use, mental health, co-occurring) and a one-way hash of the name and address that joins the two directories; names, addresses, telephones and the files themselves are never written to disk.
samhsa_nsumhss.cadence: Yearly: the 2025 directories (survey of 2024) were released on 2026-03-06. The observatory looks for a newer edition on the National Directories page and re-reads it when the data are rebuilt (python community_assets.py --refresh samhsa).
samhsa_nsumhss.used_for: Substance use and mental health treatment facilities in each municipio, in all and by type of care (community_series.json: bh_all, bh_su, bh_mh, bh_both). Counts only.
samhsa_nsumhss.terms_note: These are sensitive services, so the observatory publishes counts only: no facility name, address, telephone or point. The directories list the facilities that answered the survey and agreed to be listed; most individual practitioners are not in them. FindTreatment.gov, SAMHSA's live locator, is more current, but its API guide states no licence and speaks of 'approved users', so it is not used (wanted.json: samhsa-locator).

fpr_gii_2021.name: FPR — Global Innovation Index, Puerto Rico country profile (2021)
fpr_gii_2021.publisher: Centro de Innovación de Foundation for Puerto Rico

short.es: GII de FPR 2021

fpr_gii_2021.credit: Source: Centro de Innovación de Foundation for Puerto Rico, Global Innovation Index: Puerto Rico country profile (2021), calculated with the GII 2020 method of Cornell University, INSEAD and WIPO
fpr_gii_2021.access: FPR's two-page profile (PDF created 2021-09-26) and its working file, both internal. The profile's 80 indicators, values, ranks and marks were copied as printed into docs/analysis/gii-2021/gii_original.json on 2026-10-23; the working file was read only to explain differences. No name, email or telephone number from either file is copied.
fpr_gii_2021.cadence: A frozen snapshot: the 2021 profile does not change. Corrections are notes beside the printed values, never edits.
fpr_gii_2021.used_for: The original values, ranks 'x / 132' and marks of the Global Innovation Index page of the Knowledge Area (gii_profile.json: value, shown, rank, star, hourglass, year).
fpr_gii_2021.terms_note: FPR's own calculation, not an official WIPO ranking: Puerto Rico is not in the official Global Innovation Index. FPR has not stated a license for the profile. Some 2021 values come from proprietary sources (IHS Markit country risk, Clarivate Web of Science, Brand Finance) and are shown as FPR published them, not updated.

wipo_gii2020.name: Cornell University, INSEAD and WIPO — The Global Innovation Index 2020 (method and definitions)
wipo_gii2020.publisher: Cornell University, INSEAD and the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)
wipo_gii2020.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 IGO (report page ii); third-party data excluded

short.es: GII 2020

wipo_gii2020.credit: Cornell University, INSEAD and WIPO (2020): The Global Innovation Index 2020: Who Will Finance Innovation? Ithaca, Fontainebleau and Geneva
wipo_gii2020.access: The report and its Appendix III, read for the framework (7 pillars, 21 sub-pillars, 80 indicators), the definitions (summarized in FPR's own words) and the marks of each indicator (composite, survey, half weight, higher is worse).
wipo_gii2020.used_for: The structure and the definitions of the Global Innovation Index page (gii_profile.json), and the method behind FPR's printed ranks. No other economy's GII 2020 data are published.
wipo_gii2020.terms_note: Licensed CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 IGO: no derivatives without WIPO's permission. FPR's ranks place Puerto Rico's value among the GII 2020 values, so they derive from that edition; the page shows only Puerto Rico's values and the ranks FPR printed in 2021, and an open licence review records the question for Compliance.

wipo_gii2026.name: WIPO — Global Innovation Index 2026 database

short.es: GII 2026 de la OMPI

wipo_gii2026.credit: Source: WIPO (2026). Global Innovation Index 2026, database. Licensed CC BY 4.0. Adapted by Foundation for Puerto Rico; WIPO is not responsible for the adaptation.
wipo_gii2026.access: The database file (943,159 bytes as WIPO serves it, SHA-256 bbce0a2d...ffd73; a copy in a folder that SharePoint or OneDrive syncs gains customXml metadata parts and so another hash, which gii.py also records; downloaded on 2026-10-23 with FPR's approval) is kept in the local cache (cache/gii/2026/) and read with openpyxl in read-only mode by 'python -I gii.py --extract-2026', which keeps, for each of the 79 indicators, the screened values (no economy names), the year most economies use and FPR's checks of WIPO's method on its own data (direction, plain min-max or log transform, the range no winsorization caps, the rank rule). The extract stays in the cache.
wipo_gii2026.cadence: One edition a year (the 19th, 2026-09-29, 139 economies, 79 indicators). A new edition is read when FPR updates the page.
wipo_gii2026.used_for: The indicative GII 2026 position of Puerto Rico's updated value in 10 indicators whose source and definition match (gii_profile.json: c26_*): the number of economies with data, the year most use, the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles and Puerto Rico's place among them, written X/N. Also the threshold of the change marker (chg_thr: 5% of the interquartile range of each indicator) and the structure, method and indicator list behind 'Changes in the index since 2020' (gii_changes.json).
wipo_gii2026.terms_note: CC BY 4.0 allows reuse and adaptation with credit to WIPO, the changes marked and a statement that WIPO is not liable. Third-party data in the database are excluded from WIPO's licence, so no economy's values are republished and no economy is named: only counts, the data year, three percentiles and Puerto Rico's indicative place. A percentile can coincide with one economy's value (the median in 8 of the 10 compared indicators), without saying which. Not an official GII rank.

wb_wgi.name: World Bank — Worldwide Governance Indicators (WGI)

short.es: WGI del Banco Mundial

wb_wgi.credit: Source: World Bank, Worldwide Governance Indicators (2026 update), CC BY 4.0
wb_wgi.access: World Bank API, no key: api.worldbank.org/v2/country/PRI/indicator/{series}?source=3 for GOV_WGI_GE.EST (government effectiveness), GOV_WGI_RQ.EST (regulatory quality) and GOV_WGI_RL.EST (rule of law); read by gii.py and cached in cache/gii/.
wb_wgi.cadence: Updated once a year (last updated 2026-09-25, data to 2025). Each release revises every past year.
wb_wgi.used_for: The updated values of indicators 1.1.2, 1.2.1 and 1.2.2 of the Global Innovation Index page (gii_profile.json: upd_value, upd_year), and Puerto Rico's 2024 values for their GII 2026 position.
wb_wgi.terms_note: Perception-based composite estimates with standard errors; the World Bank advises against reading small differences between years or economies as meaningful. Because each release revises the past, values from different releases are not comparable.

wb_wdi.name: World Bank — World Development Indicators (WDI)

short.es: WDI del Banco Mundial

wb_wdi.credit: Source: World Bank, World Development Indicators, CC BY 4.0
wb_wdi.access: World Bank API, no key: api.worldbank.org/v2/country/PRI/indicator/{series} (the United States, USA, for the tariff), read by gii.py and cached in cache/gii/.
wb_wdi.cadence: Updated several times a year (last updated 2026-10-08 for the series used).
wb_wdi.used_for: The updated values of indicators 3.2.3 (NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS), 6.2.2 (IC.BUS.NDNS.ZS) and 4.3.1 (TM.TAX.MRCH.WM.AR.ZS of the United States, FPR's method), the ICT components shown beside 3.1.1 and 3.1.2, and the mirror of UNESCO series used when it is newer (gii_profile.json).
wb_wdi.terms_note: Many WDI series for Puerto Rico are blank (logistics, domestic credit, market capitalization, patents, FDI, high-tech exports). The tariff of the United States stands for Puerto Rico because the US tariff schedule applies there; it is labelled as FPR's method.

unesco_uis.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS) — Data API
unesco_uis.licence: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 IGO (CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO)

short.es: UIS de la UNESCO

unesco_uis.credit: Source: UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS), UIS Data API, February 2026 release, CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO
unesco_uis.access: UIS Data API, no key: api.uis.unesco.org/api/public/data/indicators?indicator={code}&geoUnit=PRI, read by gii.py and cached in cache/gii/.
unesco_uis.cadence: Data releases about twice a year (February 2026 for the series used).
unesco_uis.used_for: The updated values of indicators 2.1.1 (XGDP.FSGOV), 2.1.3 (SLE.1T8), 2.1.5 (PTRHC.2T3.QUALIFIED), 2.2.1 (GER.5T8), 2.2.2 (FOSGP.5T8.F500600700) and 2.2.3 (MOR.5T8.40510) of the Global Innovation Index page (gii_profile.json).
unesco_uis.terms_note: Share-alike: an adaptation must carry the same licence. The series are revised between releases, so the printed 2021 values may differ from the current ones for the same year. Inbound mobility for Puerto Rico is a UIS estimate.

imf_weo.name: IMF — World Economic Outlook (DataMapper)
imf_weo.licence: IMF copyright and usage terms: free reuse with attribution

short.es: WEO del FMI

imf_weo.credit: Source: International Monetary Fund, World Economic Outlook (October 2026), DataMapper
imf_weo.access: IMF DataMapper API, no key: imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/PPPGDP and NGDP_RPCH, read by gii.py and cached in cache/gii/ (the server refuses this project's User-Agent, so that request goes with the library's default).
imf_weo.cadence: Twice a year (April and October); the latest years are IMF estimates and the following ones projections, which gii.py leaves out.
imf_weo.used_for: The updated value of indicator 4.3.3 (GDP in PPP dollars) and the real GDP growth of the FPR estimate of 6.2.1 (gii_profile.json).
imf_weo.terms_note: The IMF allows reuse of its data with attribution, under its copyright and usage terms. Values are revised between editions: 2019 GDP in PPP dollars is 119.6 billion in the current edition, against the 126.9 billion FPR took from the October 2019 edition.

fac.name: Federal Audit Clearinghouse — single audits

more_links.label: Single audit rules (2 CFR 200, subpart F)

fac.licence: Public domain: "The data collected by the FAC is free to use and in the public domain" (FAC data page)

short.es: Federal Audit Clearinghouse

fac.credit: Source: Federal Audit Clearinghouse, US General Services Administration, single audits of the municipio governments
fac.access: FAC API (https://api.fac.gov), with a free api.data.gov key in the X-Api-Key header (FAC_API_KEY, HANDOFF decision 70; the only key the build uses, never stored in the repository or published). One request to the general table for every Puerto Rico audit (auditee_state PR, without the contact fields), then one request to the federal_awards table per fiscal year for the municipio governments' audits (first downloaded 2026-10-31).
fac.cadence: An audit is due 30 days after the auditor's report or nine months after the fiscal year ends, whichever is first, and many are late. The FAC holds audits of fiscal years 2016 onward; in the 2026-10 snapshot the observatory holds municipal fiscal years 2016 to 2025. It re-reads the list of audits only when FPR rebuilds the data (economy_series.py --fac --refresh), and downloads award lines only for fiscal years with new audits.
fac.used_for: Federal money spent by each municipio government in its fiscal year, in total, received directly or through a pass-through entity, and by federal agency (economy_series.json).
fac.terms_note: The FAC data page states that the data it collects are free to use and in the public domain (checked 2026-10-31). Audits of fiscal years 2016 to 2022 were migrated from the Census Bureau's clearinghouse to GSA in federal fiscal year 2024. The general table also holds the names, e-mail addresses and phone numbers of auditee and auditor contacts; the build never requests those fields.

lineage.en: Single audits filed by each municipio government: federal money spent in its fiscal year (July to June). The awards behind these dollars also appear in USAspending (as obligations, often to the Commonwealth) and in OpenFEMA; the stages differ, so they are never added together.

hud_lihtc.name: HUD — National Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) Database
hud_lihtc.publisher: US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Office of Policy Development and Research (HUD USER)

more_links.label: The database archive (LIHTCPUB.ZIP; saved by hand)
Missing data by year placed in service

hud_lihtc.licence: US Government work (17 U.S.C. 105: no copyright in the United States); HUD USER states no other licence for the database

short.es: Base de datos LIHTC de HUD

hud_lihtc.credit: Source: US Department of Housing and Urban Development, National Low-Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) Database, Puerto Rico
hud_lihtc.access: HUD USER answers scripts with a bot check, so the archive LIHTCPUB.ZIP is saved by hand from a browser to cache/facilities/lihtcpub.zip (HANDOFF decision 71) and the build reads LIHTCPUB.xlsx inside it. It keeps the Puerto Rico rows and these columns: the HUD project id, project name, city, state, latitude, longitude, 2020 tract and county, total and low-income units, year placed in service, construction type, credit type, the no-longer-monitored flag and the homeless and special-population targets. The street address and ZIP code are not kept.
hud_lihtc.cadence: HUD adds the projects placed in service in a year each spring (the release of 2026-05-28 covers 1987 to 2024; 2025 is due in spring 2027). Rebuilt with python facilities.py --only lihtc after a new archive is saved.
hud_lihtc.used_for: Tax credit housing projects on the 2D map and the 3D view (lihtc.geojson) and LIHTC projects, units and low-income units in each municipio (facility_series.json: lihtc_projects, lihtc_units, lihtc_li_units).
hud_lihtc.terms_note: The newer of HUD's two LIHTC sources: the eGIS layer of the same name stops at projects placed in service in 2020 (last edited 2024-12-09). HUD geocoded only some Puerto Rico projects to a point; the others carry a city only. Projects for people who are homeless or living with HIV are counted, never drawn or named.

nmtc.name: CDFI Fund — New Markets Tax Credit (NMTC) public data release
nmtc.publisher: US Department of the Treasury, Community Development Financial Institutions Fund (CDFI Fund)
nmtc.licence: US Government work (17 U.S.C. 105: no copyright in the United States); the CDFI Fund states no other licence for the file

short.es: Datos NMTC del CDFI Fund

nmtc.credit: Source: US Department of the Treasury, CDFI Fund, New Markets Tax Credit public data release
nmtc.access: The build reads the CDFI Fund's data releases page, takes the newest file named NMTC_Public_Data_Release_includes_…xlsx (the 2026-08-06 release: investments of 2001 to 2023) and reads its sheet of financial notes, one row per investment, with the project id, 2020 census tract, year, amount and state. No key.
nmtc.cadence: One release a year, in the summer, adding the investments of about three years earlier. python economy_series.py --nmtc --refresh looks for a newer file.
nmtc.used_for: Investment in low-income communities with New Markets Tax Credits by municipio and year (economy_series.json: nmtc_qlici, nmtc_projects).
nmtc.terms_note: The file also names each project's Community Development Entity and city; the observatory publishes only dollars and counts by municipio and year.

lineage.en: The CDFI Fund's public release of New Markets Tax Credit investments. Private investment made with a federal tax credit, not federal spending; kept out of spending totals.

usgs_water.name: USGS — Water Data API (reservoir water levels, river flow, groundwater levels and rainfall)
usgs_water.publisher: US Geological Survey (USGS), Water Resources Mission Area; Caribbean-Florida Water Science Center

more_links.label: USGS, Hydrologic Conditions of Selected Reservoirs in Puerto Rico
USGS Real-Time Flood Impacts (flood reference points)

usgs_water.credit: Source: US Geological Survey, Water Data for the Nation (provisional data subject to revision)
usgs_water.access: OGC API, no key: monitoring-locations (state_code 72; site_type_code LK for lakes and reservoirs, ST for streams, GW for wells), latest-continuous (parameter 72376 for reservoir levels, 00060 for river discharge, 72019 for the depth to water in a well) and daily (72375; 00060 with statistic 00003, the mean of the day; 72019). Rainfall: latest-continuous by bounding box (parameter 00045, precipitation), daily with statistic 00006 (the sum of the day) and, from the page, continuous (the 15-minute readings of the last 24 hours, as CSV). The build reads the daily values; the page reads the latest values in the visitor's browser (the API allows requests from any site). Without a key USGS limits the requests an hour and answers 429 with the seconds to wait; river_gauges.py waits and asks again. Since 2026-11-12 the river build also reads the gauge height (00065) and, where reported, the water temperature (00010) of each river gauge, and the flood reference points of Puerto Rico from USGS Real-Time Flood Impacts (api.waterdata.usgs.gov/rtfi-api/referencepoints/state/46, no key).
usgs_water.cadence: Readings every 15 minutes or so; daily values the next day. The page reads the latest when a layer is switched on; the observatory rebuilds the daily values and usual levels and flows once a month (python reservoirs.py --refresh; python river_gauges.py --refresh; python groundwater.py --refresh; python rain_gauges.py --refresh).
usgs_water.used_for: Reservoir levels (reservoirs.geojson), River flow (river_gauges.geojson), Groundwater levels (groundwater.geojson) and Rainfall (rain_gauges.geojson) on the 2D map and the 3D view.
usgs_water.terms_note: USGS marks recent data provisional. Checked 2026-11-02: 121 lake or reservoir sites in Puerto Rico, 26 with a reading in the last 30 days. Checked 2026-11-11: 1,083 stream sites in Puerto Rico, 76 with a discharge reading in the last 30 days, 71 of them with at least 8 years of daily values in 2011-2025. Checked 2026-11-12: 5,197 well sites in Puerto Rico, 34 with a depth-to-water reading in the last 30 days; 83 sites with a precipitation reading, 54 of them in the last 30 days.

nasa_black_marble.name: NASA Black Marble — VNP46A3, monthly night-time lights (VIIRS on Suomi NPP, collection 2)
nasa_black_marble.publisher: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (Black Marble team); distributed by NASA's Level-1 and Atmosphere Archive and Distribution System (LAADS DAAC)

more_links.label: Product page at LAADS DAAC (layers, quality flags, file format)
The method: Román et al. (2018), Remote Sensing of Environment 210, 113–143
The archive the build lists (for developers; downloads need a NASA Earthdata login)

nasa_black_marble.licence: NASA data from a NASA-led mission: Creative Commons Zero (CC0) unless a product is marked otherwise; NASA strongly urges users to cite the data
nasa_black_marble.credit: Source: NASA Black Marble, VNP46A3 collection 2 (https://doi.org/10.5067/VIIRS/VNP46A3.002), LAADS DAAC; Román, M.O., et al., 2018, NASA's Black Marble nighttime lights product suite, Remote Sensing of Environment 210, 113–143, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2018.03.017

The build reads one user token from the EARTHDATA_TOKEN environment variable (a GitHub Actions secret) and sends it only to LAADS; the site never calls NASA and visitors need no login (HANDOFF decision 75). nasa_black_marble.cadence: NASA posts each month about seven weeks after it ends. The observatory reads the new months when FPR runs the build (python nightlights.py, or the Night-time lights workflow).

iepr_publicos.credit: Source: Instituto de Estadísticas de Puerto Rico and Autoridad de Carreteras y Transportación, Mapa de rutas de porteadores públicos (published 2020-03-19), CC BY

iepr_publicos.cadence: Published once, on 2020-03-19, and not updated since. The portal's record is checked every 90 days; a new file needs a person to look at it before it is published.
iepr_publicos.used_for: The map layer Público routes (2020 list), and whether a público route joined each pair of municipios (transit_links.json).
iepr_publicos.terms_note: The list has no timetable, fares, operators or dates: a route on it may no longer run and newer routes are missing. The observatory shows it as a record of 2020, never as current service. Credit both the Instituto and ACT.

lineage.en: The transport authority's own list of público routes, as the statistics institute published it; the only open list of público routes with their lines.

nhtsa_fars.name: NHTSA — Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS), Puerto Rico files
nhtsa_fars.publisher: US Department of Transportation, National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), National Center for Statistics and Analysis

more_links.label: FARS downloads (one folder a year; Puerto Rico in its own subfolder)
FARS Analytical User's Manual (variables and codes)

nhtsa_fars.licence: US Government work (17 U.S.C. 105: no copyright in the United States)

short.es: FARS de la NHTSA

nhtsa_fars.credit: Source: US Department of Transportation, NHTSA, Fatality Analysis Reporting System, Puerto Rico files 2015-2024 (2024: Annual Report File)
nhtsa_fars.access: One small zip a year on static.nhtsa.gov (FARS<year>PuertoRicoCSV.zip, about 200 KB), no key; crashes.py keeps accident.csv and person.csv, cached in cache/crashes/. Years 2015-2024; the municipio (COUNTY) is given from 2020.
nhtsa_fars.cadence: NHTSA publishes each year first as an Annual Report File (about 15 months after the year) and replaces it about a year later with the final file. The newest year's file is checked every 30 days; a change needs a person to look at it.
nhtsa_fars.used_for: Fatal crashes and the people killed in them by municipio and year (pedestrians and bicyclists, motorcyclists), deaths per 100,000 residents and per 100 million vehicle-km (crashes_series.json); the deaths along each simulated connection between municipios, published only as five-year totals (transit_links.json).
nhtsa_fars.terms_note: FARS records include each crash's place, date and time. The observatory publishes only counts by municipio and year and five-year totals along a simulated connection, never a crash: the exact place and time of a death can identify a person. The Puerto Rico Traffic Safety Commission keeps its own count, which can differ from FARS.

lineage.en: NHTSA's census of fatal crashes on public roads, coded by the Puerto Rico FARS analyst from police reports, death certificates and other records.

luma_bureau.name: LUMA Energy — filings with the Puerto Rico Energy Bureau (distributed generation data and monthly metrics)
luma_bureau.publisher: LUMA Energy, filed with the Puerto Rico Energy Bureau (Negociado de Energía de Puerto Rico)
luma_bureau.licence: No licence stated (public filings with the Energy Bureau)
luma_bureau.credit: Source: LUMA Energy, filings with the Puerto Rico Energy Bureau (cases NEPR-MI-2019-0016 and NEPR-MI-2019-0007)
luma_bureau.access: Excel files linked from the Energy Bureau's case pages, no key: Exhibit 2 of the distributed generation data (quarterly) and the monthly metrics workbook 'Resumen Metricas Master'. energy_series.py reads the case pages for the newest file names. LUMA's own website bars automated access and is not used (HANDOFF decision 104 (d)).
luma_bureau.cadence: Metrics monthly; distributed generation data quarterly. The observatory rebuilds energy.json when a new file is filed (python energy_series.py --refresh).
luma_bureau.used_for: The Energy in Puerto Rico page (energy.json): production by source since 2010, rooftop solar, batteries, electricity sales and smart meters by municipio, rooftop solar by district and SAIDI.
luma_bureau.terms_note: energia.pr.gov states no terms of use and its robots.txt blocks only /wp-admin/ (checked 2026-11-13). The figures are LUMA's totals by month, municipio or district: no customer, address or installation.

eia_861m.name: EIA — Form EIA-861M, Monthly Electric Power Industry Report (sales to ultimate customers)
eia_861m.credit: Source: US Energy Information Administration, Form EIA-861M
eia_861m.access: The yearly Excel files sales_ult_cust_YYYY.xlsx (no key; the current year in xls/, older years in archive/xls/): residential revenue and sales of Puerto Rico's utility (number 15497, territory sheet) and of the states.
eia_861m.cadence: Monthly, about seven weeks after the month ends.
eia_861m.used_for: The residential price of electricity on the Energy in Puerto Rico page (energy.json: price).

fhwa_nti.credit: Source: US Federal Highway Administration, National Tunnel Inventory, through the BTS National Transportation Atlas Database
fhwa_nti.access: ArcGIS REST layer on services.arcgis.com queried with state_code_i3=72 (no key): tunnel number and name, road carried, portal point, year built and rehabilitated, daily traffic and its year, detour and length.
fhwa_nti.cadence: Yearly, with the bridge inventory; four Puerto Rico tunnels in the 2025 data.
fhwa_nti.used_for: The four road tunnels on the Bridges and tunnels map layer (bridges.geojson).

afdc_stations.name: US DOE Alternative Fuels Data Center — fuelling stations (BTS National Transportation Atlas Database)
afdc_stations.publisher: US Department of Energy, Alternative Fuels Data Center (National Laboratory of the Rockies, formerly NREL), distributed by the Bureau of Transportation Statistics (BTS) National Transportation Atlas Database (NTAD)

more_links.label: NTAD service the build reads, Alternative Fueling Stations (layer 0)

afdc_stations.licence: US Government work, available for unrestricted public use (BTS metadata)
afdc_stations.credit: Source: US Department of Energy, Alternative Fuels Data Center, through the BTS National Transportation Atlas Database
afdc_stations.access: ArcGIS REST layer on services.arcgis.com queried with state='PR' and fuel_type_code='ELEC' (no key). The direct AFDC API needs a key, so the build reads this copy, which BTS refreshes daily. The station's telephone and street address are never read.
afdc_stations.cadence: Daily at the Data Center; networks and owners report changes and the Department confirms each station.
afdc_stations.used_for: The Public EV charging stations map layer (ev_stations.geojson): public stations open or temporarily unavailable, with their ports by level, network and connectors.
afdc_stations.terms_note: The list holds the stations reported to the Data Center; it is a lower bound for Puerto Rico (26 public stations in November 2026, against 11 chargers mapped in OpenStreetMap).

cdc_svi.name: CDC/ATSDR — Social Vulnerability Index 2022
cdc_svi.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry (CDC/ATSDR), Geospatial Research, Analysis, and Services Program

more_links.label: About the index and its four themes

cdc_svi.licence: US federal government data; the page states no licence and gives a suggested citation
cdc_svi.credit: Source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention/Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry/Geospatial Research, Analysis, and Services Program. CDC/ATSDR Social Vulnerability Index 2022 Database, Puerto Rico, downloaded November 2026
cdc_svi.access: Two CSV files, no key: Puerto Rico's counties (municipios) and Puerto Rico's census tracts (svi.cdc.gov/Documents/Data/2022/csv/). The build keeps the overall rank and the ranks of three themes; the estimates behind them stay in CDC's files.
cdc_svi.cadence: CDC publishes an edition every two years; 2022 is the newest (the 2024 address answered 'not found' on 2026-11-14). The observatory rebuilds by hand when a new edition comes (python svi.py --refresh after changing the edition).
cdc_svi.used_for: The Social Vulnerability Index of each municipio (svi_series.json: svi_overall and three themes) and of each census tract (svi_tract.json).

un_wpp.publisher: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division

un_wpp.access: Two public CSV files, no key: the abridged life tables (WPP2024_Life_Table_Abridged_Medium_1950-2023.csv.gz, about 145 MB) and the demographic indicators (about 17 MB); the build streams them and keeps Puerto Rico's rows (location 630).

un_wpp.used_for: Puerto Rico's life table by sex, 2010-2019, for the estimate of net migration by age (netmig_age_series.json), and the UN's net migration for its check.
